posts.title: Appearance: Friends of Griffin 8
posts.description: Yesterday, I joined my frenemy buddy D. Griffin Jones on his new show, Friends of Griffin . And, because Griffin is not an old fogey like me, we did this… on video . 😱 During the episode, we discussed the plethora of Apple announcements from the last week, and then spent a fair bit of time discussing our new iPhone Duo s. It’s rare I have the occasion to get on video, so if you want to see as well as hear me talk, this would be a great occasion to do so. Plus, the conversation was quite fun, irrespective of how you consume it. Read on Liss is More

posts.title: Appearance: The Incomparable 840
posts.description: Ted Lasso was an absolute gift to the world during the pandemic. When everything felt like it couldn’t get much worse, Ted Lasso was a ray of positive, optimistic sunshine. The show — particularly the first season — meant a lot to many, including and especially me. After the three-season arc wrapped, we all assumed that, eventually, Apple would find a number that would get Jason Sudeikis to agree to do the show again. Lo and behold, that happened, and we now have Ted Lasso Season 4 . I joined a whole bunch of panelists to discuss the season as a whole. As every one of my appearances on The Incomparable goes, this episode was hugely fun and terribly intimidating. As always, I had a great time recording it, and if you’re a Lasso fan, I think you’ll enjoy the listen. If you want an episode-by-episode breakdown of season four, you should also check out Football is Life , also on The Incomparable. Read on Liss is More

posts.title: A Quick Trip to New York
posts.description: I very much admire the writing of Matt Haughey ; in particular, his trip logs. For example, this one detailing his trip to Japan was incredible. There’s been a lot of chatter about where and how to share things amongst my peers recently, and I’ve been thinking about where, how, and why I share things. It seems to me that the best answer available to me — better than a nominally photo-oriented service owned by a jerk — better than a short-form text-based service owned by a truly sadistic monster — better even than a network owned by nobody — is to post it here. [1] Call me an old man — a shoe that fits ever-better with each passing day — but I think I should probably post to the web more, and walled gardens less. Even if those gardens’ walls are quite permeable. So, with that in mind, I wanted to talk about a trip I took this week.
